newsitem.title: VIRGIN ISLANDS: Virgin Islands economy starting to stabilize - gov.
newsitem.headline: Virgin Islands economy starting to stabilize - gov.

text.p: U.S. Virgin Islands Gov. Roy Schneider said the islands' construction industry is healthy and its tourism economy has begun to rebound from a series of devastating hurricanes.
That assessment was one of the few points of optimism in Schneider's state-of-the-territory address Monday night.
Schneider, a doctor, described the islands' economy as a patient who is in serious condition but has begun to stabilize.
The U.S. territory in the Caribbean suffered a large revenue drop due to Hurricane Marilyn in September 1995 and has since been unabled to meet many obligations.

Schneider said the territory owes $59 million in income tax refunds, $20 million in vendor payments, $111 million in back wages to government employees, $13 million in current wages, and $44 million on a federal disaster loan from Hurricane Hugo in 1989.

He did not mention the $85.6 million owed for a federal disaster loan from Hurriance Marilyn, but said the territory would draw down the balance of the $127.2 million federal disaster loan authorized after that hurricane.
Schneider said the sale of part of the Water and Power Authority will provide money to pay off government debts, but did not specify an amount.

Schneider said he hopes to raise additional revenues by developing a trans-shipment port at the container port on St. Croix and revising gaming laws to make the territory more attractive to casino investors.
He said the government is also working to increase rum exports from St. Croix to increase rum excise tax revenues retrned to the territory.
Schneider said he has cut allotments to all government departments and agencies by more than 10 percent, curbing the use of cellphones, travel and motor vehicles.
"We are already saving at the annual rate of more than $1 million and there is more to come," he said.
